## Development Seeder Implementation

The seeder assumes the Development schema was already migrated to the current
revision. For a new local database the developer applies the current
migrations first; application startup then populates the empty schema.

### Dataset shape

Cover the main meaningful states and relationships, for example where
applicable: newly created; active or in progress; completed; inactive or
archived; entities with and without optional values; with and without optional
relationships; representative status values; meaningful boundary states. Do not
attempt every combination. When the required entity graph or scenarios are
complex, the task requirements should describe the dataset explicitly rather
than leaving Claude to invent a large generic object graph.

### Seeder example

Use one or more representative root/anchor entities to detect existing data.

| Scenario | Default technique |
|---|---|
| Read-only entity query | `AsNoTracking()` when useful |
| Read model | Database-side projection |
| Primary-key entity lookup | `FindAsync` when its semantics fit |
| Complex entity graph | Explicit `Include` / projection |
| Set-based mass update/delete | `ExecuteUpdateAsync` / `ExecuteDeleteAsync` when appropriate |
| Normal query | Ordinary LINQ |
| Measured extremely hot query | Consider a compiled query |
| Multiple commits requiring atomicity | Explicit transaction |
| Production schema change | Reviewed migration script, controlled deployment |
| Empty Development database | Run the maintained development seeder |
| Need a fresh local seed dataset | Recreate the local database explicitly |

## API Client Generation

When OpenAPI client generation is adopted, treat generated code as generated,
keep it separate from handwritten feature logic, and regenerate it when the API
contract changes. Backend contract documentation: `swagger` skill.

## Testing

Test frontend behavior at the appropriate level: meaningful component behavior,
validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior, complex
reactive state. Do not test Angular framework internals. E2E tests focus on a
small number of important user workflows unless the project requires broader
E2E coverage, and the same behavior is not duplicated at every test level. Use
the test runner configured in `package.json`.

When versions coexist, test meaningful differences: version routing,
version-specific response shape, a deprecated version still operational during
its support period, unsupported-version behavior, and shared Application
behavior staying consistent where intended. Do not duplicate identical tests
because two versions share Application behavior.

Application Services can be unit-tested by replacing repository and
external-service abstractions with controlled test doubles. Focus assertions on
the use-case result and meaningful side effects. A verification such as
"repository method X was called once" is useful only when that interaction is
part of the contract; it is not the default assertion style. When important
behavior depends heavily on EF Core semantics, transactions, DI wiring,
serialization, or HTTP, prefer an integration test over reproducing the stack
with mocks.
